q: How many players does one soccer team have on the field, including the goalkeeper?
x: Each side fields ten outfield players and one goalkeeper. A team must keep at least seven players on the field to continue a match.

q: Which city hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics?
x: The opening ceremony took place at the Bird's Nest stadium on 08/08/08 at 8:08 pm, a date chosen because 8 is a lucky number in China.

q: On which surface is the Wimbledon tennis tournament played?
x: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam still played on natural grass. Players are also required to wear almost entirely white clothing.

q: How many interlocking rings appear on the Olympic flag?
x: The five rings represent the five inhabited continents joined together. The flag was introduced in 1914 and first flown at the 1920 Games.

q: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
x: Uruguay hosted and won the first tournament, beating neighbors Argentina 4-2 in the final in Montevideo.

q: In golf, what is a score of one stroke under par on a hole called?
x: The term 'birdie' comes from early American slang, where 'bird' meant something excellent. It was coined around 1899 in Atlantic City.

q: Michael Jordan won six NBA championships with which team?
x: The Bulls won two separate runs of three straight titles, in 1991-93 and 1996-98. Jordan was Finals MVP every time.

q: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football?
x: A touchdown is worth six points, and the team can then try for one or two extra points. Before 1912 a touchdown was worth only five points.

q: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
x: Athens was chosen to honor the ancient Games' Greek origins. About 240 athletes from 14 nations took part.

q: How many holes are played in a standard full round of golf?
x: The standard of 18 holes was set at St Andrews in Scotland in 1764, when the club reduced its course from 22 holes to 18.

q: Which sport is played with a shuttlecock?
x: Badminton is named after Badminton House in England, where the game became popular in the 1870s. Its feathered shuttlecock traditionally has 16 feathers.

q: What color card does a referee show to send a soccer player off the field?
x: Cards were introduced at the 1970 World Cup after English referee Ken Aston got the idea while stopped at a traffic light.

q: How many players from each team are on the court at once in basketball?
x: Each team can use more than five players in a game through substitutions, but only five may be on the court at a time.

q: Sumo wrestling is the traditional national sport of which country?
x: Sumo has been practiced in Japan for well over a thousand years and has Shinto religious roots. Bouts are often over in a few seconds.

q: What is the official distance of a marathon?
x: The exact distance is 26 miles 385 yards, or 42.195 kilometers. It was standardized after the 1908 London Olympics.

q: How many bases are there on a baseball diamond, counting home plate?
x: Runners must touch first, second and third base in order before reaching home plate to score. The bases are 90 feet apart.

q: What was the birth name of the boxer Muhammad Ali?
x: He won Olympic light heavyweight gold in 1960 as Cassius Clay. He changed his name in 1964 after joining the Nation of Islam.

q: The Tour de France is a famous race in which sport?
x: The first Tour de France was held in 1903. The race lasts about three weeks and covers more than 3,000 kilometers.

q: Sprinter Usain Bolt represents which country?
x: Bolt won the 100 m and 200 m at both the 2008 and 2012 Olympics. He grew up in Trelawny, Jamaica, and first loved cricket.

q: In which sport do two packs of forwards push against each other in a scrum?
x: The scrum is a way of restarting play after a minor rule break. In rugby union each pack has eight forwards.

q: Which Olympic sport features events on the pommel horse and rings?
x: These are two of the six apparatuses in men's artistic gymnastics. Gymnastics has been part of every modern Olympic Games since 1896.

q: How many players are in a cricket team on the field?
x: Each side fields eleven players, including the wicketkeeper. Only two batters from the batting team are on the field at a time.

q: Which country hosted the 2014 FIFA World Cup?
x: It was Brazil's second time hosting the men's tournament, after 1950. Germany beat Argentina 1-0 in the final at the Maracana.

q: Which city hosted the 2012 Summer Olympics?
x: London became the first city to host the modern Summer Games three times, after 1908 and 1948.

q: In which sport do teams compete in the Super Bowl?
x: The first Super Bowl was played in January 1967. The winner receives the Vince Lombardi Trophy.

q: Which Olympic medal is awarded for second place?
x: At the first modern Olympics in 1896 winners received silver medals and runners-up got bronze. Gold medals for winners began in 1904.

q: Which team sport awards the Stanley Cup?
x: The cup was donated in 1892 by Lord Stanley, the Governor General of Canada. Each winning team engraves its players' names on it.

q: In which country did the sport of cricket originate?
x: Cricket was played in southern England by the 16th century. The first international match was played in 1844 between the United States and Canada.

q: Tennis star Roger Federer comes from which country?
x: Federer was born in Basel in 1981. He won Wimbledon eight times over his career.

q: Against which team did Diego Maradona score his 'Hand of God' goal in 1986?
x: Minutes later in the same quarter-final he scored a famous solo goal after dribbling past most of the England side. Argentina won 2-1.

q: How long is a standard professional soccer match, not counting stoppage time?
x: A match is two halves of 45 minutes each, with a short break at halftime. Referees add stoppage time for delays.

q: How many players per team are on the court in a volleyball match?
x: Teams rotate positions each time they win the serve. Volleyball was invented in 1895 in Massachusetts.

q: In tennis scoring, what does the term 'love' mean?
x: The word likely comes from the French 'l'oeuf', meaning egg, because a zero looks like an egg. This origin story is popular but not fully proven.

q: What is the maximum score in a single game of ten-pin bowling?
x: A perfect game requires twelve consecutive strikes. Each frame can score up to 30 when strikes follow strikes.

q: What shape is a standard boxing ring?
x: Despite the name 'ring', the ring is square, with ropes on four sides. The name comes from the earlier circles drawn by spectators.

q: Which swimming stroke is most commonly used in freestyle events?
x: Freestyle lets swimmers use any stroke, but the front crawl is by far the fastest, so everyone chooses it.

q: In which sport might you see a triple axel?
x: The axel is the only common figure skating jump that takes off facing forward, so a triple axel has three and a half rotations.

q: What does the Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' mean?
x: The Latin motto was proposed by Pierre de Coubertin and adopted in 1894. It was proposed by a friend, Father Henri Didon.

q: In which Greek location is the Olympic flame lit before each Games?
x: The flame is lit using a parabolic mirror and the Sun's rays, then carried by relay to the host city. The torch relay began in 1936.

q: The 'All Blacks' is the nickname of which country's national rugby union team?
x: The team is famous for performing the haka before matches. They wear an all-black uniform with a silver fern emblem.

q: The Masters golf tournament is held each year at which course?
x: The winner is awarded a green jacket. The course is in Augusta, Georgia, and is famed for its azaleas.

q: Which small principality hosts a famous Formula One street race through its city?
x: The Monaco Grand Prix has been held since 1929 and is part of the unofficial Triple Crown of Motorsport.

q: Lionel Messi was born in which country?
x: Messi was born in Rosario, Argentina, and moved to Barcelona at age 13. He won the Ballon d'Or several times before 2015.

q: How many Grand Slam tennis tournaments are played each year?
x: They are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open. Winning all four in one calendar year is called a Grand Slam.

q: What is it called when a soccer player scores three goals in one match?
x: The term began in cricket, where a bowler who took three wickets in a row was awarded a new hat. It was later adopted by other sports.

q: In golf, what is it called when a player sinks the ball in one stroke from the tee?
x: The odds of an ordinary golfer making a hole-in-one on a given par-3 are around 12,000 to one.

q: In which sport do England and Australia compete for the Ashes?
x: The Ashes series began in 1882, after a newspaper joked that English cricket had died and its ashes would be taken to Australia.

q: In which sport is a home run scored?
x: A home run usually happens when the batter hits the ball over the outfield fence in fair territory, allowing everyone to circle the bases.

q: Which Spanish city hosted the 1992 Summer Olympics?
x: The 1992 Games were the first with NBA players in the US basketball team, known as the Dream Team.

q: Which Australian city hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics?
x: Australia has hosted the Summer Games twice, in Melbourne in 1956 and in Sydney in 2000.

q: Which US city hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics?
x: The 1996 Games marked the 100th anniversary of the modern Olympics. Muhammad Ali lit the Olympic cauldron.

q: Which South Korean city hosted the 1988 Summer Olympics?
x: The Seoul Games included table tennis and tennis as full medal sports, the latter returning after a 64-year break.

q: Which Japanese city hosted the 1998 Winter Olympics?
x: Nagano was the second Japanese city to host the Winter Games, after Sapporo in 1972.

q: Which Canadian city hosted the 2010 Winter Olympics?
x: Vancouver's Games were held in February 2010. Calgary had earlier hosted the 1988 Winter Olympics.

q: Which two countries co-hosted the 2002 FIFA World Cup?
x: It was the first World Cup held in Asia and the first with two hosts. Brazil beat Germany 2-0 in the final.

q: Which African country hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup?
x: It was the first World Cup held on the African continent. The tournament is remembered for the loud sound of the vuvuzela horn.

q: Which country won the 2006 FIFA World Cup in Germany?
x: Italy beat France on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the Berlin final. It was Italy's fourth World Cup title.

q: Which country won the 2010 FIFA World Cup?
x: Andres Iniesta scored the winning goal in extra time of the final. It was Spain's first World Cup title.

q: Which country won the 1966 FIFA World Cup on home soil?
x: England beat West Germany 4-2 after extra time at Wembley. It remains England's only men's World Cup title.

q: How many strikes make an out for a batter in baseball?
x: The same batter also walks to first base after four balls. 'Three strikes and you're out' became a common saying in everyday English.

q: How high above the floor is a regulation basketball hoop?
x: The hoop has been 10 feet (3.05 m) high since Dr James Naismith nailed a peach basket to a gym balcony in 1891.

q: How many players are in a rugby union team on the field?
x: Rugby league has 13 players, and rugby sevens has seven. Union teams are split into eight forwards and seven backs.

q: How many players per team, including the goalie, are on the ice in a standard ice hockey game?
x: Each team normally has five skaters plus a goaltender on the ice. Penalties can temporarily reduce a team's numbers.

q: How many gold medals did swimmer Michael Phelps win at the 2008 Beijing Olympics?
x: Phelps broke Mark Spitz's single-Games record of seven golds from 1972. One of his wins came by just 0.01 seconds in the 100 m butterfly.

q: Which gymnast scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history, in 1976?
x: Comaneci was only 14. The scoreboard could not display a 10.00, so it showed 1.00 instead.

q: Which American sprinter won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics?
x: Owens won the 100 m, 200 m, long jump and 4x100 m relay. His triumphs in Berlin disproved Nazi claims of racial superiority.

q: What color jersey does the Tour de France race leader wear?
x: The yellow jersey was introduced in 1919. It was chosen because the newspaper that organized the race was printed on yellow paper.

q: Who invented basketball in 1891?
x: Naismith was a Canadian-born physical education teacher in Springfield, Massachusetts. He wrote the original 13 rules of the game.

q: The Kentucky Derby is a famous event in which sport?
x: It has been run at Churchill Downs in Louisville since 1875. The race lasts only about two minutes, earning it the nickname 'the most exciting two minutes in sports'.

q: In which sport do teams slide granite stones toward a target called the house?
x: Curling originated in Scotland in the 16th century. Teammates sweep the ice in front of the stone to guide it.

q: Judo originated in which country?
x: Judo was founded in 1882 by Jigoro Kano and became an Olympic sport in 1964. The name means 'the gentle way'.

q: Taekwondo, a martial art and Olympic sport, originated in which country?
x: Taekwondo emphasizes high kicks. It became an official Olympic sport at the Sydney Games in 2000.

q: How often is the men's FIFA World Cup normally held?
x: The tournament has been held every four years since 1930, except in 1942 and 1946, when it was cancelled because of World War II.

q: Which country had won the men's soccer World Cup five times by 2014?
x: Brazil won in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002. It is the only team to have played in every World Cup tournament.

q: What color is a standard tennis ball in major professional tournaments?
x: Yellow balls were introduced in 1972 because they are easier to see on television. Wimbledon adopted them in 1986.

q: In baseball, what is the name of the player who throws the ball to the batter?
x: The pitcher throws from a raised mound 60 feet 6 inches from home plate. Fastballs can exceed 100 mph.

q: In which country is the Wimbledon tennis tournament played?
x: Wimbledon is held at the All England Club in southwest London. It is the oldest tennis tournament in the world, first played in 1877.

q: Which surface is used for the French Open tennis tournament?
x: The red clay courts at Roland Garros slow the ball and produce a higher bounce, making long rallies common.

q: Babe Ruth is a legend of which sport?
x: Ruth began as a pitcher for the Boston Red Sox before becoming a legendary slugger for the New York Yankees. He was nicknamed 'the Sultan of Swat'.

q: Which city hosted the 1984 Summer Olympics?
x: The 1984 Games were a financial success, run mostly with private funding and existing venues.

q: The football clubs Real Madrid and Barcelona play in the top league of which country?
x: Their rivalry is known as El Clasico. The top Spanish league is called La Liga.

q: In which country do clubs like Manchester United and Arsenal play?
x: The English Premier League started in 1992. English football clubs have a history that dates back to the 1800s.

q: How many points is a free throw worth in basketball?
x: Free throws are awarded after certain fouls and are taken from the free throw line 15 feet from the backboard.

q: How many points is a try worth in rugby union?
x: A try is scored by grounding the ball over the opponents' try line. It was worth only one point in the 1870s.

q: What is the cricket term for a batter being dismissed without scoring a run?
x: The term comes from the shape of the digit 0, which resembles a duck's egg. Being out first ball is called a golden duck.

q: What may outfield soccer players not deliberately touch the ball with during play?
x: Only the goalkeeper, inside their own penalty area, may handle the ball. Throw-ins are the other time hands are used.

q: Which swimming stroke is named after an insect?
x: Butterfly evolved from breaststroke in the 1930s and became its own Olympic event in 1956.

q: In soccer, what is the name of the box-shaped area in front of each goal where a keeper can use their hands?
x: Fouls by defenders inside this area result in a penalty kick. It extends 18 yards from the goal line.

q: Which country won the 1998 FIFA World Cup on home soil?
x: France beat Brazil 3-0 in the final in Paris. Zinedine Zidane scored twice with his head.

q: In which Australian city is the Australian Open tennis tournament held?
x: The tournament is played at Melbourne Park in January, the height of the Australian summer.

q: In which sport do competitors race around gates in a slalom event?
x: Skiers must pass between pairs of poles in the correct order. Missing a gate means disqualification.

q: How many players does a baseball team have on the field when playing defense?
x: These are the pitcher, catcher, four infielders and three outfielders. Some leagues add a tenth fielder known as a designated hitter at bat only.

q: How long is an Olympic-size swimming pool?
x: The pool is also 25 meters wide and at least 2 meters deep. Shorter 25-meter pools are used in short-course competitions.

q: What is the name for a score of two strokes under par on a golf hole?
x: After the 'birdie' became popular, golfers chose a larger bird for the next-lower score. An 'albatross' is three under par.

q: Which weight division is the heaviest in professional boxing's traditional classes?
x: Heavyweight boxers have no upper weight limit. Champions in this division have often been regarded as the toughest men in sports.

q: How many periods are played in a standard ice hockey game?
x: Each period lasts 20 minutes in professional games. Tied games may go to overtime or a shootout.

q: Which track and field event involves throwing a heavy metal ball?
x: The men's Olympic shot weighs 7.26 kg (16 lb). It must be pushed from the shoulder, not thrown like a baseball.

q: Brazil's national soccer team is famous for wearing which color shirt?
x: The famous yellow shirt was introduced after the 1950 World Cup loss, when the old all-white kit was dropped following a design contest.

q: Which Olympic event combines swimming, cycling and running?
x: The triathlon made its Olympic debut at the 2000 Sydney Games. The standard Olympic distance is a 1.5 km swim, 40 km ride and 10 km run.

q: In which sport are the terms 'deuce' and 'advantage' used?
x: Deuce means the game is tied at 40-40, and a player must win two points in a row to take the game.
